description: Master Plant Development Agreement with Google (Oct 2024): a US fleet of KP-FHR plants totalling 500 MW by 2035, first plant by 2030; Kairos builds, owns and operates and sells power under PPAs. Deal amount; Hermes 2 is the first deployment under it
PPA with TVA (Aug 2025) for up to 50 MW from Hermes 2 in Oak Ridge, operation targeted 2030; Google takes the clean attributes; first US utility PPA for a Gen IV reactor

Amazon agreement (Oct 2024, restated in the 2026 IPO prospectus): options for more than 5 GWe of Xe-100 projects in the US by 2039 if fully exercised; first project four units / 320 MWe with Energy Northwest (expandable to 960 MWe). Lower bound of X-energy's total
Centrica joint development agreement (Sep 2025): up to twelve 80 MWe Xe-100 at Hartlepool, first electricity in the mid-2030s (year 2035 used for 'mid-2030s'; not an exact stated year)
Centrica and X-energy aim at a UK fleet of about 6 GWe (76 reactors in 19 four-packs); no target year stated
IPO prospectus (2026): pipeline of more than 11 GWe / 144 reactors across the US and UK assuming customers exercise their contingent rights in full; no year stated (the Amazon part is by 2039)

Dow / Long Mott Energy: four Xe-100 at Seadrift Texas (about 320 MWe); NRC review expected to finish late 2026 with construction permit expected Q1 2027; the prospectus gives no operation year (the 2023 announcement aimed at completion by the end of the decade)
Meta agreement (Jan 2026): Meta funds early development of two Natrium units (345 MWe each) with delivery of initial units as early as 2032; 690 MW = 2 x 345 MW

Meta agreement (Jan 2026): up to eight Natrium plants (two funded plus rights to energy from up to six more), up to 2.8 GW baseload (up to 4 GW with molten-salt storage boost); TerraPower gives no year for the full eight (Meta frames its whole nuclear programme as up to 6.6 GW by 2035)
Q2 2026 10-Q: deployment of the first Aurora powerhouse (Aurora-INL 75 MWe) targeted in 2028
Meta prepayment agreement (Jan 2026) for a 1.2 GW Aurora campus in Pike County Ohio; first phase as early as 2030; full 1.2 GW by 2034
Non-binding Master Power Agreement with Switch (Dec 2024): 12 GW of Aurora powerhouse projects through 2044, binding agreements to follow project by project
Equinix: pre-agreement (2024) for up to 500 MW from Aurora powerhouses under 20-year PPAs, restated by Equinix Aug 2025; non-binding; no year stated
Customer pipeline above 14 GW after the Switch agreement (Dec 2024), almost all non-binding; no year stated
CEO goal of 1 GW of Aalo reactors online by the end of this decade (year 2030 used for 'end of decade')

Planned 1 million sq ft 'GigaWatt Factory' to come online by 2028; company states its factories produce 1 GW per year per million sq ft (at least a hundred 10 MWe reactors a year at full capacity); current Austin pilot factory is 40,000 sq ft. Factory procurement began 2026 per aalo.com/factory

R-50 microreactor factory at Oak Ridge: first mass-produced Kaleidos delivered to customers in 2028, then scaling to up to 50 reactors per year; 50 MW/yr = 50 units x 1 MWe (stated in units not MW); NRC accepted the factory application May 2026
Equinix pre-order (Aug 2025) of 20 Kaleidos microreactors of about 1 MWe each; no delivery year stated
Equinix pre-order power agreement for about 500 MWe from Stellaria's fast-spectrum molten-salt Stellarium reactors in Europe; Stellaria targets first fission 2029 and commercial production 2035

BN-1200M at Beloyarsk unit 5: preparation stage started Jul 2025, first concrete planned 2027, completion targeted 2034 under the Russian general scheme for power facilities; adds to BN-600, BN-800 and BREST-OD-300 (statement amount only)
Westinghouse and Prodigy plan a first transportable eVinci microreactor station (up to 5 MWe) in Canada by 2030 for a remote mine (statement from 2024; not reconfirmed since)
In its Q2 2026 results (2026-08-12) Fervo raised its long-term development target by 100 MW, to 1.1 GW by 2030, and says it is preparing to put more than a gigawatt online by the end of the decade

Fervo says it holds more than 1 GW of binding PPAs across its portfolio (Oct 2026; the S-1 of Apr 2026 had 658 MW). Fervo gives no delivery year for the total; 2030 is the latest stated COD among the contracted projects (Cape Station 2026-2028, Corsac 2030). The Fall 2026 investor deck reportedly says 1,054 MW (deck not readable, HTTP 403)

Alongside the 396 MW Google PPA, Fervo gives Google an option to expand by about 600 MW by June 2030, close to 1 GW for Google alone. That is a lower bound for Fervo's total, since other buyers' PPAs come on top; the option is not binding on Google

Geothermal Framework Agreement with Google Energy (2026-03-19): structures possible offtake of up to 3 GW by the end of 2033 for Google data centres. The S-1 risk factors call it non-binding, although another section calls it binding
Ormat targets 100 MW of operating EGS in 2030-2031, conditional on pilot drilling, permits, PPAs and FIDs; year = end of the window
Ormat targets 1 GW of EGS by 2033-2035 (stated as a target, not a commitment); year = end of the window
United Downs (3 MW, online Feb 2026) plus two more Cornwall sites for a further 10 MW by 2030; 13 = the sum of the two stated figures

FY2023 10-K states installed production capacity of two gigawatts per year (headcount ~800 in 2023). Conflicts with the FY2025 10-K, which puts Fremont at ~1 GW/yr before the 2026 expansion; probably building nameplate vs equipped run rate.
FY2025 10-K: Fremont annual production capacity approximately 1 GW (run rate) before the expansion announced in 2025.

FY2025 10-K: doubling Fremont run-rate capacity from 1 GW to 2 GW by end-2026 (so 2027 = first full year), supported by federal tax credits; 2026 10-Qs add capacity investment at Fremont and Delmarva (Delaware) without a new GW figure.

Gunsan (Saemangeum) SOFC plant on Ceres steel-cell technology, 50 MW/yr, completed Jun 2025, mass production of stacks and 300 kW systems from end-Jul 2025 (Doosan IR 2026 decks; Ceres H1-2025 interim).

Weichai, Ceres licensee (new stationary SOFC licence 5 Nov 2025, Shandong), targets 200 MW of SOFC capacity by end-2027 (Ceres H1-2026 results as reported by AJ Bell; not checked against the RNS). Weichai says batch capacity should land within 2026; no shipped MW.
ELCO I factory near Tallinn opened Sep 2025, raising cell/stack capacity from 10 to 360 MW/yr (~50 m EUR capex + 25 m EUR EU Innovation Fund). Capacity is shared between SOFC and SOEC; no split.
Trade press (Sep 2025): ambition of 1 GW/yr within two years of the ELCO I opening; MEDIUM confidence, not in the primary release.
2017 plan to ramp the Mezzolombardo (Italy) plant to 50 MW/yr (~16,000 units/yr) from 2020; not confirmed as built. 2023 company slides claim 75 MW/yr of solid-oxide (electrolysis-labelled) capacity.
Hope Gas programme 7,250 x 2 kW WATT HOME units over three years from Jan 2026; earlier WATT fleet small and not quantified (medium confidence).
Form Factory 1 (Weirton WV) to reach annual output of at least 500 MW of batteries by 2028; at the 100 h product duration this is ~50 GWh/yr (conversion). Stated on the factory page.
Oct 2024 expansion announcement: expansion completed by end 2025, annual production capacity of 500 MW by 2028 with at least 750 workers.
MIT Technology Review (Oct 2026) puts current factory output capacity at 2 GWh per year; converted at 100 h = 20 MW/yr. Year = time of statement (current capacity).

Crusoe strategic capacity agreement (Mar 2026) for 12 GWh of iron-air systems for AI data centres, reserved volume/pricing/delivery terms, deliveries from 2027, end year and sites not stated; 12 GWh at 100 h = 120 MW (conversion). Value is this agreement's volume, not company total. Year left empty because no completion year is stated.

Form reports about 80 GWh promised under commercial agreements (Oct 2026; was ~20 GWh at start of 2026, >75 GWh in Mar 2026); 80 GWh at 100 h = 800 MW (conversion). Includes Pine Island 30 GWh, Crusoe 12 GWh, Lincoln 8.5 GWh and others; roughly a third is not itemised publicly. No delivery year stated.
Oct 2025: Form had over 200 MW of batteries under contract, about 200 MW in finalised contracts (snapshot, no delivery year).

Google / Xcel Energy Pine Island agreement (Feb 2026): 300 MW / 30 GWh; first modules by end 2028, phased online 2028-2031 (MIT TR); pending MPUC approval (decision early 2027). Value is this agreement's volume.

Company homepage states an annual production capacity of 1 GW / 4.5 GWh (so ~4.5 h systems; MW as stated). Start year not given (page undated, read 2026-11-08). Homepage also states 3.9 GWh+ installed globally; Rongke releases of Jul 2025 and 31 Dec 2025 say more than 3.5 GWh deployed.

Its automated 'Xing G' manufacturing base is said to reach 2 GW / 8 GWh per year of V-STAR stacks and systems at full output (duration 4 h as implied by the company figures); year of full output not stated in the source (article Nov 2025).
First Gyeryong plant (completed May 2023) has 330 MWh/yr; converted at 4 h (duration not stated). Identity with H2 Inc. (Korea) not confirmed by the source.
Second Gyeryong plant due 2H 2026 lifts total output to 1.2 GWh/yr (this is the total, not an increment); converted at 4 h (duration not stated).

company: Dalian Hengrong New Energy / CNNC Huineng Henan
description: Zhoukou (Henan) flow battery industrial base: construction of a 500 MW/2 GWh per year VRFB stack and system-integration line started 5 Jan 2025 (co-investors incl. CNNC Huineng Henan, Zhoukou state capital); first output year not stated.

More than 190 MWh of systems deployed, contracted or awarded across 90+ sites in 17 countries (company overview Sep 2025); converted at 4 h (duration not stated). Excludes the 1.5 GWh FlexBase design selection.

Company pipeline (Oct 2026): over 2 GWh operating or contracted; converted at the 10 h standard unit = ~200 MW (conversion). Snapshot, no year. Exceeds the ~1.2 GWh itemised in projects.csv, so some contracted projects are not public.
Company pipeline (Oct 2026): over 3 GWh of projects authorised (permitted); at 10 h = ~300 MW (conversion). Snapshot, no year.
Company pipeline (Oct 2026): development pipeline above 30 GWh across four continents; at 10 h = ~3,000 MW (conversion). Snapshot, no year.
